canonical_statement: Let (M,g) be a smooth Riemannian manifold with its Levi-Civita connection and let gamma be a C2 curve. In any smooth coordinate chart containing the image under consideration, gamma is a geodesic exactly when each coordinate component satisfies d2 gamma^k/dt2 + sum over i,j of Gamma^k_ij(gamma(t)) (d gamma^i/dt) (d gamma^j/dt) = 0. A regular locally length-minimizing curve satisfies this equation after constant-speed parametrization; no claim is made that every complete geodesic is globally minimizing.
domain_and_universes: M is a finite-dimensional smooth real manifold; g is a Riemannian metric; gamma maps a real interval to M and is C2. Exact Lean universes, model-with-corners data, interval representation, and coordinate conventions remain open.
quantifiers: gamma : C2 curve on a real interval
a smooth coordinate chart containing the curve segment
hypotheses: the connection is the Levi-Civita connection of g
gamma is twice differentiable on the segment
the selected chart contains the segment being expressed
constant-speed parametrization is required when deriving the equation from local length minimization
conclusion: The intrinsic autoparallel condition is equivalent to the displayed Christoffel-symbol coordinate equations; regular locally minimizing curves in constant-speed parametrization obey them.

excluded_degenerate_cases: No assertion that arbitrary parametrizations satisfy the affine geodesic equation, that every geodesic globally minimizes length, or that a single chart covers an arbitrary whole curve. Constant curves may satisfy the intrinsic equation but are excluded from the regular length-minimizer implication. Pseudo-Riemannian free-particle dynamics belongs to THM-P-0639, not this target.
